facts_of_case: The husband filed a petition under Section 12 (1) (c) and (d) of Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 seeking dissolution of marriage. The trial court dismissed the petition by Order dated 27.08.2003. The present appeal has been preferred.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party seeking dissolution of marriage to prove that the respondent has not been living with him as his wife for at least three years immediately preceding the presentation of the petition.
legal_principles.held: It is settled law that the burden lies on the party seeking dissolution of marriage to prove that the respondent has not been living with him as his wife for at least three years immediately preceding the presentation of the petition.

legal_principles.principle: The court will not grant a divorce unless it is satisfied that the respondent has not been living with the petitioner as his wife for at least three years immediately preceding the presentation of the petition.
legal_principles.held: This Court holds that the court will not grant a divorce unless it is satisfied that the respondent has not been living with the petitioner as his wife for at least three years immediately preceding the presentation of the petition.

outcome.final_order: The Civil Miscellaneous Appeal stands dismissed for non-prosecution. No order as to costs.
